rules.explain: Cloud Run pulls the container image from Artifact Registry, so an ECR image is copied there first; the image itself is not rebuilt.
rules.quote: Google recommends the use of Artifact Registry.

rules.explain: Cloud Run sends requests to one port on the container and injects it as the PORT environment variable; the ECS container port becomes that port.
rules.quote: By default, requests are sent to 8080, but you can configure Cloud Run to send requests to the port of your choice.

rules.explain: The ECS entry point and command become the Cloud Run command and args, overriding the image defaults the same way.
rules.quote: If you want to override the image's default entrypoint and command arguments, you can use the command and args fields in the container configuration.

rules.explain: Cloud Run can run sidecar containers, but only one receives traffic and start order must be declared; confirm each extra container is still needed on Cloud Run.
rules.quote: To specify container start up order in a sidecar deployment, you use the container dependencies feature.

rules.explain: Cloud Run runs Linux x86_64 containers only; an ARM64 (Graviton) or Windows image must be rebuilt for x86_64 Linux before it can run.
rules.quote: Cloud Run specifically supports the Linux x86_64 ABI format.

rules.explain: Cloud Run sets CPU and memory per instance; the Fargate task size maps to a documented Cloud Run pair, rounding CPU up to at least 1 vCPU so the sub-1-vCPU constraints never apply.
rules.quote: A minimum of 0.5 vCPU is needed to set a memory limit greater than 512MiB.

rules.explain: This CPU and memory pair is outside the combinations the Cloud Run documentation lists.
rules.quote: Cloud Run instances that exceed their allowed memory limit are terminated.

rules.explain: The load balancer's HTTP health check path becomes a Cloud Run startup probe on the same path.
rules.quote: Startup probes determine whether the container has started and is ready to accept traffic.

rules.explain: ECS runs a shell command inside the container as its health check; Cloud Run probes are HTTP, TCP, or gRPC only, so the check must be re-expressed as an endpoint.
rules.quote: You can configure HTTP, TCP, and gRPC probes using Google Cloud console, YAML, or Terraform:

rules.explain: Plain environment variables carry over unchanged.
rules.quote: You can set a maximum of 1000 environment variables for a Cloud Run service.

rules.explain: AWS Secrets Manager and SSM references become Secret Manager references pinned to a version; the runtime service account needs the Secret Accessor role, and you add the values yourself.
rules.quote: Environment variables are resolved at instance startup time, so if you use this method, Google recommends that you pin the secret to a particular version instead of using latest as the version.

rules.explain: Cloud Run can mount an NFS share such as Filestore, but without file locking and with a 30-second mount budget at startup; v1 omits the volume because no Filestore exists yet.
rules.quote: Cloud Run does not support NFS locking. NFS volumes are automatically mounted in no-lock mode.

rules.explain: The task reached private resources through VPC subnets; Cloud Run does the same with Direct VPC egress, but a Google Cloud VPC holding those resources must exist first, so v1 omits it.
rules.quote: You can enable your Cloud Run service, function, job, or worker pool to send traffic to a VPC network by using Direct VPC egress with no Serverless VPC Access connector required.

rules.explain: Cloud Run scales to zero when idle unless minimum instances are set; the ECS desired count becomes the minimum, and those instances are billed while idle.
rules.quote: With minimum instances set, Cloud Run keeps at least the number of minimum instances running, even if they're not processing requests.

rules.explain: Cloud Run closes a request that gets no response within the timeout; the documented default is used because ECS has no equivalent field.
rules.quote: The timeout is set by default to 5 minutes (300 seconds) and can be extended up to 60 minutes (3600 seconds).

rules.explain: This task runs on a schedule and exits; on Cloud Run that is a job triggered by Cloud Scheduler, not a service, and v1 only deploys services.
rules.quote: Unlike a Cloud Run service, which listens for and serves requests, a Cloud Run job only runs its tasks and exits when finished.

rules.explain: This task exposes no port and runs continuously; on Cloud Run that is a worker pool, not a service, and v1 only deploys services.
rules.quote: Handles always-on background workloads such as workloads from message queues (Kafka, Pub/Sub, RabbitMQ).

rules.ecs_field: taskRoleArn policy actions and AWS SDK clients in source
rules.explain: Cloud Run runs as a Google service account, which carries no AWS credentials; every AWS service the code still calls needs its own plan before this service can work.
rules.quote: In Cloud Run, the service identity is a service account that is both a resource and a principal.
